blockers: The live shop wins on the thing the business actually sells. Painted Earth is a gallery and craft shop whose strength is photography of real work by named makers; the prototype must show every artwork as a drawn placeholder tile, because republishing 92 third-party makers' catalogue photography has no recorded licence. Eight identical mountain-and-sun tiles cannot be offered to this owner as an improvement on their own gallery pages, and the imagery policy that makes the prototype honest is the same policy that makes it unpublishable.
improvements: The surviving case — collection-only and shipping-quote terms visible before the Add to Cart button, and a route forward from a sold original — is real and narrow. If the shop is ever approached, offer it as a merchandising fix to their existing product template, not as a website transformation.

The four creative-workshop products are all unavailable and the waiting list is run by hand in a sold-out product description. That is a smaller, more fixable problem than anything in the original-art loop.
